title: cerinthe major subsp. gymnandra
intro: Cerinthe major subsp. gymnandra, commonly known as Honey Flower, is a plant species in the borage family, Boraginaceae, characterized by its unique, drooping, or nodding flowers. The Honey Flower has been traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat various health issues, including digestive problems, inflammation, and anxiety, due to its health benefits in soothing the digestive system, reducing inflammation, and promoting relaxation. The therapeutic actions of Cerinthe major subsp. gymnandra are attributed to its ability to act as an anti-inflammatory, antispasmodic, and anxiolytic agent, which helps to calm the nervous system and alleviate stress. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
